speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. To begin our assessment, could you please tell me how many weeks pregnant you are and describe the severity and location of your abdominal pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old woman, gravida 2, para 1, at 38 weeks' gestation. The patient reports experiencing vaginal bleeding for the past hour accompanied by severe abdominal pain. She mentions that she felt contractions before the onset of the bleeding, but the contractions ceased once the bleeding began. Her first childbirth was a cesarean section due to nonreassuring fetal heart rate.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of a prior cesarean section, the sudden onset of severe abdominal pain followed by vaginal bleeding at 38 weeks is highly concerning for uterine rupture. I need to assess the fetus's well-being immediately; can you tell me if you are currently feeling any fetal movements?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Vaginal bleeding. I also have Severe abdominal pain, History of contractions that stopped, Previous cesarean delivery.

speaker: Doctor
text:
I need to assess the baby's current status immediately; please tell me if you are feeling any fetal movements right now or if the baby has become less active.
